title: Relative Clauses: who, which, that
grammarNote:
Относительные придаточные (relative clauses) добавляют информацию о существительном. Отвечают на вопрос "Какой? / Который? / Кто именно?"

WHO — для людей:
"The student who answered first got bonus points."
"I met a professor who speaks seven languages."

WHICH — для вещей и животных:
"The book which I recommended is now a bestseller."
"The laptop which broke down was under warranty."

THAT — для людей И вещей (в определительных клаузах):
"The car that I want is too expensive." (= which)
"The student that won is from our group." (= who)

WHOSE — принадлежность:
"The student whose essay was best got an A."

WHERE — место:
"The university where I study is in Uralsk."

WHEN — время:
"I remember the day when we first arrived at WKU."

📍 Структура: NOUN + relative pronoun + информация
"The professor WHO TEACHES linguistics is brilliant."

grammarTable.subject: who

grammarTable.subject: which

grammarTable.subject: that

grammarTable.subject: where
grammarTable.example: The library where I study is very quiet.

grammarTable.subject: whose
grammarTable.example: He's a writer whose books sell millions.

grammarTable.subject: Defining
grammarTable.example: "The film that I watched was amazing."

grammarTable.subject: Non-defining
grammarTable.example: "October Sky, which is a true story, is inspiring."

rows.form: She is a teacher who inspires students.
He is the student who won the scholarship.
They are the directors who made the film.
I know a girl who speaks five languages.
He is someone who always keeps his promises.
She is an author who writes about human emotions.
It's a book which changed my perspective.
The cinema which we went to last week is closed.
She uses an app which helps her study vocabulary.
That's the building which was designed by a famous architect.
He published an article which received many responses.
It's a documentary which every student should watch.
It's a story that everyone can relate to.
He's someone that I respect deeply.
It was a film that made me cry.
It's an experience that I will never forget.
She's a person that you can always trust.
It's a topic that interests all of us.
The library where I study is open until 10 p.m.
That's the café where they filmed the interview.
She is an author whose books are read worldwide.
He's the professor whose class I enjoy the most.
This is the room where Dr. Akhmetov holds his workshops.
The actor whose performance I loved was in three films.

grammarTip: RULES: who = people | which = things/animals | that = both (informal) | where = places | whose = possession. In DEFINING relative clauses (essential info), you can omit "that/which/who" when it's the object: "The film (that) I watched was amazing." BUT you can't omit the subject: "She is a student who loves reading." ✅

exercises.text: She is a writer ___ has won many awards.

exercises.instruction: Complete with who, which, or that.
exercises.text: It's a film ___ changed the way I see the world.
exercises.hint: "that" or "which" can be used for things. Both are correct here.

exercises.text: This is the library ___ I study every evening.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct relative pronoun.
exercises.text: He is a director ___ films are loved around the world.
It's a novel ___ explores the theme of friendship.
exercises.hint: "which" = relative pronoun for things (a novel is a thing).

exercises.text: "She is a student which loves reading" is correct.
exercises.hint: Use "who" for people: "She is a student who loves reading."

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct relative pronoun.
exercises.text: The professor ___ teaches English at WKU is very inspiring.

exercises.instruction: Identify what the relative pronoun refers to.
exercises.text: In "That's the building that was built in 1990," "that" refers to:
exercises.hint: "that" refers to "the building" — a thing, not a person or place.
"that" can replace "who" or "which" in informal defining relative clauses.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct relative pronoun.
exercises.text: This is the café ___ they filmed the famous documentary.
Which sentence uses a relative clause correctly?
opts: She is a student who loves reading.
She is a student which loves reading.
She is a student whom loves reading.
She is a student where loves reading.
exercises.correct: She is a student who loves reading.
exercises.hint: "who" for people as subject of the relative clause.

exercises.text: "It's a book that I recommend" has a defining relative clause.
exercises.hint: "that I recommend" = defining relative clause (no commas, identifies which book).

questions.text: "who" in relative clauses is used for:
She is a student ___ works hard every day.

questions.hint: "which" = relative pronoun for things and animals.

questions.text: It's a book ___ I recommend to all my friends.
questions.hint: "that" can be used for both people and things in defining relative clauses.

questions.text: "She is a teacher which inspires students" is correct.
questions.hint: Use "who" for people: "She is a teacher who inspires students."

questions.text: That's the cinema ___ we always watch films.

questions.hint: "whose" shows possession: the writer whose books are famous.
"that" can replace "which" in defining relative clauses (informal/neutral).

questions.text: He is an author ___ books are read in 30 countries.
What is "The Kite Runner" about, according to Kamila?
opts: A boy who dreams of becoming an astronaut
A friendship tested by betrayal and redemption
An empire that falls through war
questions.correct: A friendship tested by betrayal and redemption
questions.hint: Paragraph 2: "a novel that tells the story of a friendship that is tested by betrayal and redemption."
Paragraph 5: "a documentary that examines the impact of social media on mental health and democracy."

questions.text: Dr. Akhmetov says students should only read books that are easy and enjoyable.
questions.hint: Paragraph 6: "Read books that challenge you… A book that makes you uncomfortable often changes you the most."

questions.text: "Novel" in the context of literature means:
The book is about ___ — the main character betrays his best friend.
questions.hint: "Betrayal" = the act of being disloyal or breaking someone's trust.

opts: Examine information carefully and draw conclusions
questions.correct: Examine information carefully and draw conclusions
questions.hint: "Analytical" = related to the ability to analyse, examine, and draw conclusions from information.
